about.title: Livermore Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Livermore sits at the eastern edge of Alameda County, and a large share of its traffic funnels onto a single freeway. Public collision records show I-580 eastbound and westbound carrying the highest counts in the city, with Isabel Avenue following behind. In 2025, the most recent final crash year, Livermore recorded 364 injury collisions. Those crashes hurt 486 people and took 5 lives. The pattern is fairly predictable: reports peak on Fridays between 5 p.m. and 7 p.m., as the workweek winds down. If you were among the people injured, you may now be sorting through doctor visits, a damaged vehicle, and calls from another driver's insurer asking for a recorded statement. You are not required to give one. We handle Livermore car accident cases on a contingency basis, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery. California gives most claimants two years to file, but photos, witnesses, and repair records fade far sooner.
about.commonInjuriesTitle: Injuries Common in Livermore Car Crashes

items.title: Deadlines Are Shorter Than Most People Think
items.desc: California allows two years for most car accident claims, but if a city, county, or Caltrans vehicle was involved, a government claim may be due in as little as six months. We can calendar the correct deadline from day one.

items.title: Partial Fault Does Not End Your Claim
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover even if you share some blame for the crash; your compensation is simply reduced by your percentage. There is also no cap on non-economic damages such as pain and lost quality of life.

items.title: No Upfront Cost, No Recorded Statement Pressure
items.desc: We work on contingency, so nothing is owed unless your case produces a recovery. We also handle the other insurer for you, which means you can decline that recorded statement without feeling cornered.

items.question: I was hit on I-580 near the Isabel Avenue exit. Does it matter that it happened on a freeway?
items.answer: Freeway crashes often involve multiple vehicles, higher speeds, and CHP rather than Livermore Police as the reporting agency. That changes where your collision report lives and who the witnesses might be. We can request the CHP report, dashcam footage, and any Caltrans camera data before it is overwritten.

items.question: The other driver's insurance company keeps calling me. Do I have to talk to them?
items.answer: No. You have no legal obligation to give the other insurer a recorded statement, and doing so can lock you into details you later remember differently. Politely tell them your attorney will be in touch, then let us manage those conversations.

items.question: How long do I have to file a car accident claim in Livermore?
items.answer: For most collisions between private drivers, California gives you two years from the crash date. If a government vehicle or a road maintenance issue is involved, a formal claim may need to be filed within six months. Because the clock varies by defendant, it helps to get the right answer for your situation early.
